/**
 * @name Dangerous Built-ins Usage
 * @description Detects usage of dangerous built-in functions like eval, exec, and pickle.
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity error
 * @id py/dangerous-builtins
 * @tags security
 *       external/cwe/cwe-502
 *       external/cwe/cwe-094
 *       external/cwe/cwe-078
 */

import python
import semmle.python.ApiGraphs

from DataFlow::CallCfgNode call
where
  (
    call = API::builtin(["eval", "exec"]).getACall() or
    call = API::moduleImport("pickle").getMember(["load", "loads", "dump", "dumps"]).getACall() or
    call = API::moduleImport("marshal").getMember(["load", "loads"]).getACall() or
    call = API::moduleImport("shelve").getMember("open").getACall() or
    call = API::moduleImport("os").getMember(["system", "popen"]).getACall() or
    call = API::moduleImport("subprocess").getMember(["call", "run", "Popen"]).getACall()
  )
select call, "Usage of dangerous function."
findings.hypothesis: The package might be using dangerous built-ins like eval, exec, or pickle for serialization or dynamic execution, which could lead to RCE.

findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name Unsafe Reflection
 * @description Using getattr/setattr with user-controlled attribute names can lead to unauthorized access or modification.
 * @kind path-problem
 * @problem.severity warning
 * @id py/unsafe-reflection
 * @tags security
 *       external/cwe/cwe-915
 */

import python
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.DataFlow
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.TaintTracking
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.RemoteFlowSources
import semmle.python.ApiGraphs

module ReflectionConfig implements DataFlow::ConfigSig {
  predicate isSource(DataFlow::Node source) {
    source instanceof RemoteFlowSource or
    source instanceof DataFlow::ParameterNode
  }

  predicate isSink(DataFlow::Node sink) {
    exists(DataFlow::CallCfgNode call |
      (
        call = API::builtin("getattr").getACall() or
        call = API::builtin("setattr").getACall() or
        call = API::builtin("delattr").getACall()
      ) and
      sink = call.getArg(1) // The attribute name argument
    )
  }
}

module ReflectionFlow = TaintTracking::Global<ReflectionConfig>;
import ReflectionFlow::PathGraph

from ReflectionFlow::PathNode source, ReflectionFlow::PathNode sink
where ReflectionFlow::flowPath(source, sink)
select sink.getNode(), source, sink, "Unsafe reflection using attribute from $@.", source.getNode(), "user input"
findings.hypothesis: Unsafe usage of getattr/setattr with user-controlled input.

/**
 * @name Identify Reflection Context
 * @description Find the function and code surrounding the reflection finding
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity medium
 * @id py/reflection-context
 */

import python
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.DataFlow

from DataFlow::CallCfgNode call, Function f
where
  call.getLocation().getFile().getShortName() = "__init__.py" and
  call.getLocation().getStartLine() = 353 and
  call.getScope() = f
select call, "Reflection in function " + f.getName()

/**
 * @name Inspect __getattr__ implementation
 * @description Retrieves the source code of the __getattr__ method in cachetools/__init__.py to understand the context of the reflection.
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity medium
 * @id py/inspect-getattr
 * @tags inspection
 */

import python

from Function f, Class c
where 
  f.getName() = "__getattr__" and
  f.getEnclosingModule().getName().matches("%cachetools%") and
  f.getScope() = c
select f, c.getName()
findings.hypothesis: Inspect the code around the identified reflection to determine if it exposes internal attributes dangerously.
